description: Large rectangular enclosure that was identified and dated by pottery to the mid-1st CE to the end of the 4th CE. The site has produced a great many finds, including over 500 coins, 40 brooches, lion-head studs, a silver ring, and a sceptre handle of a type also found at Wanborough Temple. It was thought that a Roman temples could be on the site, but none have been identified so far.
bibliography: Hall. “Stratton Farm, Godstone, Surrey: Archaeological Evaluation and Assessment of Results,” 2007.
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Stratton Farm, Godstone (Surrey).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
